course.title: CS 101: Systems Programming & Operating Principles

sections.title: Section 1: Architecture & Execution Models
sections.description: Hardware foundations, register files, cache hierarchies, and instruction pipelining.

lessons.title: 1.1 Memory Hierarchy & CPU Registers
lessons.description: Examines L1/L2/L3 caches, register sets, and latency numbers every programmer should know.

blocks.title: Lecture: Hardware Foundations & The Memory Wall

blocks.content:
### Latency Numbers Every Systems Engineer Should Know

Accessing CPU registers occurs in less than **1 cycle (~0.5 ns)**. In contrast, retrieving data from **L1 Cache** requires approximately 4 cycles (1 ns), **L2 Cache** roughly 10 cycles, and **Main RAM** between 60–100 ns.

lessons.title: 1.2 Concurrency, Threads & Race Conditions
lessons.description: Understanding mutexes, semaphores, atomic operations, and memory barriers.

blocks.content:
### Critical Sections and Mutex Locks

A **data race** occurs when two or more concurrent threads access the same memory location concurrently without synchronization.
